title: GM MARINE NAV. LTS ALARM SYSTEM

composition.serve_who: Sheet GMMS 108'-111b is titled "GM MARINE NAV. LTS ALARM SYSTEM" and shows (1) the NAV.LIGHT ALARM MODULE MK3-1 (a purpose-built annunciator with Plug A/B/C for lamp status inputs, alarm-panel indicator lamps, mute switch S25 and a sounder), whose function is to monitor/alarm nav-light circuits — this is 690-lts-nav-em (Lights — nav em / registered mapping "NAV. LIGHTS -> 690-lts-nav-em"); and (2) the relay bank (Re7-Re13) + terminal strip T/S E/F that actually switches and feeds the individual nav/steaming light loads (PORT/STBD/STERN/AUX PORT/AUX STBD/AUX STERN NAV. LT., STEAMING LT.1/2) — these load names map directly to 690-navigation-lights per the engineer-confirmed mapping list. The main-panel NAV. LIGHTS I/II and STEAMING LIGHTS I/II selector switches (feeding Plug A pins 5-8, terminals 38-41) belong to the vessel control panel infrastructure (641-vessel-control-panel), not to the lights themselves. The Siemens 3UG4621-1AW30 block sits beside the PORT/STBD NAV LT loads and is treated as a monitoring/protective relay for that circuit per prior open question q1/q75 (still unresolved as to exact coil feed).

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: This is the module drawn inside the dotted enclosure, titled 'NAV.LIGHT ALARM MODULE MK3-1 GM MARINE SERVICES'; register mapping list ties NAV. LIGHTS to 690-lts-nav-em. The module's alarm/indicator function (mute switch, per-lamp status indicators, sounder) is distinct from the physical nav lights themselves.

functions.label: Per-circuit lamp-status indication (RED1/GREEN1/WHITE1/RED2/GREEN2/WHITE2/STEAMING1/STEAMING2)
functions.what_it_does: Displays on the ALARM PANEL IND. lamp bank which nav-light circuit (port/stbd/stern x2 sets, steaming x2) is reporting status, via Plug A pins 1-8 feeding individual indicator lamps returning to a common NEG bus (Plug A pin 9).

flow_scenarios.path: Each status line (Plug A[1..8]) -> its named indicator lamp -> common bus -> Plug A[9] NEG

functions.dry_data: 24V DC low-current indicator lamps; module labelled MK3-1

functions.label: Audible alarm sounding with mute
functions.what_it_does: Drives an external alarm/horn device off Plug A group; the S25 pushbutton mutes the sounder via Plug A pin 10 to the common bus.

flow_scenarios.path: Alarm condition on any status line -> internal logic -> ALARM device terminals [1]/[2] energised -> sounder active
Operator presses S25 -> Plug A pin 10 -> common bus -> mute logic silences sounder

functions.dry_data: ALARM device + feed side not traced on this sheet (positive/feed side of the sounder is not drawn — only its + and - terminal labels shown); see uncertainty.
functions.sheet_region: ALARM device top-left of sheet, PLUG A pin 10/S25 in module box

functions.label: External plug connections (Plug B, Plug C) to remote/other circuits
functions.what_it_does: Plug B (10 pins, pins 9/10 marked +) and Plug C (4 pins) provide external interconnects from the module — Plug C ties to relay-bank C1-C4 contact group per netlist; Plug B continues off-sheet.

flow_scenarios.path: Plug C pins 1-4 <-> external wiring to relay bank contact group (C1-C4) region; Plug B pins continue off-crop, not traced further on this sheet

functions.dry_data: Plug B pins 9/10 marked + supply per legend
functions.sheet_region: module enclosure, Plug B/Plug C symbol rows

equipment_groups.equipment_name: Navigation & Steaming Lights (PORT/STBD/STERN/AUX PORT/AUX STBD/AUX STERN NAV. LT., STEAMING LT.1/2)
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Each load is individually named on the sheet and directly matches the engineer-confirmed mapping list entries (PORT NAV. LT., STBD NAV. LT., STERN NAV. LT., AUX PORT/STBD/STERN NAV. LT., STEAMING LT.1/2 all -> 690-navigation-lights). Established fact 690-navigation-lights already documents E22-E37 terminal assignment for these exact loads, consistent with this sheet.

functions.label: PORT/STBD/STERN + AUX nav light supply and switching via relay bank Re7/Re8 and Re12
functions.what_it_does: Switches +21 supply (T/S E terminal 21, fed from main panel — cross-reference) through relays Re7/Re8/Re12 to terminal strip T/S E terminals 22-33, which individually feed PORT, STBD, STERN, AUX PORT, AUX STBD, AUX STERN nav lamps. NAV. LIGHTS I/II selector on the main panel (Plug A pins 5/6, terminals 38/39) determines whether the primary or auxiliary nav-light set is selected via Re7/Re8 contacts feeding into the shared C1/C2/C3 relay-contact block controlled by Re12.

flow_scenarios.state: NAV. LIGHTS switch position I (primary set)
flow_scenarios.path: Main panel NAV.LIGHTS I -> Plug A[5] -> terminal 38 -> Re7 relay contact circuit -> C1 contact block -> Re12 contacts -> T/S E terminals 22/24/26 -> PORT/STBD/STERN NAV. LT. -> common return at 23/25/27/29/... bus

flow_scenarios.state: NAV. LIGHTS switch position II (auxiliary set)
flow_scenarios.path: Main panel NAV.LIGHTS II -> Plug A[6] -> terminal 39 -> Re8 relay contact circuit -> C2 contact block -> Re12 contacts -> T/S E terminals 28/30/32 -> AUX PORT/AUX STBD/AUX STERN NAV. LT.

functions.dry_data: Supply origin T/S E terminal +21; Re7/Re8/Re12 coil feed/return sides are each INCOMPLETE on this sheet (see uncertainties) — function is understood (switch primary vs aux set) even though exact coil polarity is not fully traced here.

functions.label: Steaming lights supply and switching via relay bank Re9/Re10/Re13
functions.what_it_does: Switches supply through Re9/Re10/Re13 and C4 contact block to T/S E terminals 34-37, which continue via multi-core cable MU5-12 (established fact 690-navigation-lights: 'also 10/34 & 11/36 STEAMING LTs GMMS 112') to T/S F terminals 51/52 feeding STEAMING LT.1 and STEAMING LT.2 respectively.

flow_scenarios.path: Main panel STEAMING LIGHTS I -> Plug A[7] -> terminal 40 -> Re9 relay contact -> C4 contact block -> Re13 contacts -> T/S E terminal 34 -> MU5-12[10] -> T/S F terminal 51 -> STEAMING LT.1
Main panel STEAMING LIGHTS II -> Plug A[8] -> terminal 41 -> Re10 relay contact -> C4 contact block -> Re13 contacts -> T/S E terminal 36 -> MU5-12[11] -> T/S F terminal 52 -> STEAMING LT.2

functions.dry_data: Positive/feed side of STEAMING LT.1 and STEAMING LT.2 not traced on this sheet — only the return path via T/S F 51/52 is drawn (incomplete).
functions.sheet_region: Re9/Re10 lower relay column and Re13/C4 block; T/S F small terminal group (~0.76-0.80, 0.83-0.87)

functions.label: Monitoring relay on PORT/STBD nav lamp circuit (Siemens 3UG4621-1AW30)
functions.what_it_does: A Siemens 3UG4621-1AW30 relay/contactor block is drawn adjacent to the PORT/STBD NAV. LT. loads with IN A1+/M A2- coil terminals and contact 11-12 (NO, dotted 11-14 unused). Per prior engineer answers on other sheets (q1/q75 remain open specifically for this sheet), its exact role (separate protective trip vs monitoring input) is not settled here.

flow_scenarios.path: IN A1+ -> coil supply (not traced back to a breaker on this sheet); M A2- -> return (not traced); contact 11->12 available for switching an external circuit (destination not drawn)

infrastructure.system_name: Main Panel selector switches & terminal strip feed (T/S E +21, Plug A pins 5-8, terminals 38-41)
facts: NAV. LIGHTS I/II selector switch and STEAMING LIGHTS I/II selector switch are drawn at main panel, feeding Plug A pins 5,6,7,8 which land on terminals 38,39,40,41 respectively — these are control inputs to the relay bank, not the lights themselves.

T/S E terminal +21 is the supply feed point into the relay bank (Re7-Re10) coil circuits; origin breaker/panel for +21 is not shown on this sheet (cross-reference to main panel wiring GMMS 112 per established fact 641-vessel-control-panel).

T/S E terminals 22-37 form the output terminal strip distributing to each named nav/steaming light; MU5-12 multi-core cable continues terminals 34-37 to T/S F 51/52 per established fact 690-navigation-lights (GMMS 112).

uncertainties: Re7, Re8, Re9, Re10, Re11, Re12, Re13 coil energising paths: only one side (typically the contact/switching side) is traced to T/S E terminals or main-panel switch terminals on THIS sheet; the coil's positive feed and negative return are not both fully traced here (this differs from the settled XA41/XA60 answer which applies to a different Re7-Re11 relay bank on a hydraulic sheet — that settled answer must NOT be applied to this nav-lights sheet's Re7-Re13, which are a different equipment context).

ALARM sounder device (horn/buzzer) positive and negative supply terminals [1]/[2] are drawn but the conductor's origin/destination beyond the module enclosure is not traced — one side genuinely incomplete.
STEAMING LT.1 and STEAMING LT.2 positive/feed side is not traced on this sheet — only the return path via T/S F 51/52 back through MU5-12 to T/S E 34/36 is drawn.

Siemens 3UG4621-1AW30 relay's exact functional role (protective trip vs monitoring input for PORT/STBD nav circuit) and its coil feed source are not resolved on this sheet — this is the same open question (q1/q75) carried from prior extraction, still unanswered here.

Correspondence between PLUG A pins 1-8 (RED1/GREEN1/WHITE1/RED2/GREEN2/WHITE2/STEAMING1/STEAMING2 indicator labels) and which specific physical nav-light circuit (PORT vs STBD vs STERN vs AUX-x) each pin actually monitors is NOT measured on this sheet — the netlist does not bind these labels to the T/S E terminal nets; do not assume RED1=PORT etc. by naming convention alone.
